report.title: opencode.nvim implementations compared, with a vanilla Vim 9.1 implementation plan

repositories.name: sudo-tee/opencode.nvim
repositories.role: Full-featured Neovim chat client and IDE frontend

repositories.name: nickjvandyke/opencode.nvim
repositories.role: Small prompt/context/event bridge that leans on native editor UX

report.audience: An engineer planning a vanilla Vim 9.1 port that does not depend on Neovim, Lua, or optional Neovim plugins.
report.summary: The two plugins represent opposite ends of the design space. sudo-tee builds a persistent, stateful chat application inside Neovim: panel tabs, a reducer over SSE, a renderer for tool/reasoning/Markdown parts, rich context de-duplication, V2 diff review with inline comments, and quick-chat inline edits. nickjvandyke deliberately stays thin: it discovers/starts a server, captures context through placeholders, submits prompts through existing input/select UI, forwards events as autocmds, reloads edited files, and reviews edits with native :diffpatch. A Vim 9.1 port should not attempt a literal translation of sudo-tee. The pragmatic path is a nick-style core (transport, context, prompt, operator, events, permissions, diff) with a sudo-tee-style layered architecture, then a panel/streaming renderer as a second phase. Vim 9.1 provides all the essential primitives (job_start, timers, JSON, text properties with virtual text, popup menus, signs, diff mode, User autocmds), but it lacks Neovim's extmarks/Treesitter/LSP ecosystem and its Lua convenience layers. The main engineering risks are SSE parsing and reconnect, asynchronous UI state, transcript rendering performance, and OS-specific clipboard/base64 handling.

what_to_reuse_from_sudo_tee: Layered separation: transport -> protocol adapter -> observation/state -> UI.
Command intent model where Ex commands, keymaps and API calls share handlers.
Context de-duplication and a context bar that shows what will be sent.
Session diff review flow and inline-comment-to-prompt loop.
Tool formatter registry concept (with a smaller built-in set).
Server lifecycle ideas: configured URL is authoritative; native service first; legacy spawn fallback.
what_to_reuse_from_nickjvandyke: Placeholder context syntax and longest-match-first substitution.
Operator implementation with g@ for ranges and dot-repeat.
Minimal server discovery via service.json + configured URL + start callback.
SSE heartbeat deadline and reconnect behavior.
Promise-free core that is easy to reason about.
User autocmd event surface for user automation.
Optional integration policy: bridge glue in docs, core enhancements in the plugin.
what_not_to_copy_directly: Neovim extmarks, Treesitter, vim.diagnostic, vim.ui.select, vim.lsp, vim.uv and vim.schedule assumptions.
The full sudo-tee feature surface in the first release; it multiplies UI and protocol risk.
A Promise/async-await port. Vim 9.1 has no coroutines; callback state machines are clearer.
A dependency on snacks/telescope/blink. The Vim9 port should expose native hooks instead.
Render-markdown-style inline rendering in phase one.
A literal per-token full transcript rebuild; it will flicker and lose folds.

design_implications: Use a normal input buffer for the panel. input() blocks the event loop, so streaming would stop while composing.
Use a scratch output buffer with text properties. Batch writes and debounce with timer_start.
Keep a central callback registry rather than promises. Represent requests as ids with success/error handlers and a timeout timer.
Prefer curl for all HTTP, including SSE. Raw ch_open is viable for plain TCP but TLS is the blocker.
Treat the SSE parser as a small state machine: accumulate chunks, split frames on blank lines, handle ':' comments as heartbeats.
Use popup_menu/popup_create for pickers and permissions; use complete()/completefunc for input completion.
Use native diff mode and :diffpatch for review. Do not build a custom diff renderer in phase one.
Expose a stable OpencodeEvent:<type> autocmd surface with a documented g: event dict.

recommended_target.name: vim-opencode.vim
recommended_target.strategy: A Vim9-native, V2-first, layered client. Start with a small bridge core (transport, discovery, context, prompt, operator, events, permissions, diff), then add a split-panel transcript and session tabs.
why: It captures the highest-value workflows early: prompt with context, run commands, see events, approve permissions, review edits.
It keeps the first release small enough to test on Vim 9.1.
It preserves a clean path to sudo-tee-like features without committing to a full application port.
It avoids Neovim-only abstractions from day one.

in_scope_v1: Server discovery/start/connect with basic auth and directory scoping.
HTTP request layer and SSE subscription with heartbeat/reconnect.
Select menu for prompts and server commands.
Permission dialogs and single-file edit diff review.
Optional split panel with streaming output (phase 2).
deferred: Internal panel tabs and project-group persistence.
Inline review comments and session-diff file trees.
Tool formatter registry and rich reasoning/tool folds.
explicit_non_goals: Provide an LSP server for completion.
Drive the OpenCode TUI as an undocumented control surface.

principles: Core knows nothing about windows and buffers.
One transport abstraction for requests and streams.
One protocol adapter interface; V2 implementation first.
One event reducer that produces UI-agnostic session state.
UI is a consumer of state and an emitter of intents.
Every public action is available as an Ex command and a function.

transport.requests: job_start(['curl', '-sS', '--fail-with-body', '-o', bodyfile, '-w', '%{http_code}', '-D', headerfile, ...]) with a timeout timer; on exit read files and decode JSON.
transport.stream: job_start(['curl', '-sS', '-N', ...]) with out_cb; accumulate chunks and parse SSE frames.
transport.auth: Basic auth via --user; headers via -H; x-opencode-directory for V2.
transport.why_not_ch_open: ch_open supports TCP but not TLS; curl handles HTTPS, proxies and redirects.
transport.backpressure: Queue requests; limit concurrent curls; cancel by job_stop on timeout/shutdown.
transport.error_model: Return a dict {ok, status, body, error}; callbacks get the same shape.

async.model: Callback registry keyed by request id plus timer-based timeouts; no promises or coroutines.
patterns: request(id, spec, OnSuccess, OnError) registers handlers and starts curl.
SSE heartbeat timer resets on every event/comment; expiry triggers reconnect with capped backoff.
UI updates are deferred with timer_start(0, ...) when called from job callbacks.
Cancellation marks the request id dead and stops the job; late callbacks are ignored.

ui.panel: Vertical split: output on top, input at bottom. Scratch buffers with buftype=nofile, bufhidden=hide, noswapfile. Input is a normal editable buffer; output is nomodifiable outside render batches.
ui.input: Buffer-local mappings: <CR> submit (normal), <S-CR> submit (insert if terminal supports), <C-c> cancel, <Tab> pane switch, @/~/ /# gestures, Up/Down history. Completion via complete() from TextChanged or <C-x>.
ui.output: Line-oriented text with prop_add for highlights and virtual text, sign_place for comments, manual folds for tools/reasoning. Timer-debounced batch updates.
ui.pickers: popup_menu() for short lists; a custom popup buffer for filtering/preview/multi-select. If a fuzzy finder is available, an optional adapter can call it.
ui.dialogs: popup_create() for permission/question dialogs; inputlist() for simple choices; input() for one-shot text.
ui.markdown: syntax/markdown.vim plus conceal; custom syntax for tool headers, code fences and diffs. No Treesitter.
ui.notifications: echomsg/echoerr plus optional popup_notification; avoid blocking dialogs during streaming.

protocol.phase_1: V2 only: GET /api/info, GET/POST/DELETE /api/session*, GET /api/event, commands, permissions, diff.
protocol.phase_2: Add a V1 adapter with /global/health, /session*, /global/event and legacy permission/question paths.
protocol.normalization: Adapters return shared session/message/part/event shapes; UI never sees raw V1/V2 differences.

persistence.validation: Skip missing directories and deleted sessions on restore; never fail startup because a snapshot is stale.

implementation_pathways.name: Skeleton, configuration and command surface
implementation_pathways.goal: A loadable Vim9 plugin with config, commands, completion, logging and a test harness.
steps: Create plugin/vim-opencode.vim with a load guard, :Opencode command, -nargs/-range/-complete=custom, and default mappings behind a flag.
Create config.vim: defaults dict, deep-merge, validation, keymap tables, XDG path helpers.
Create util.vim: JSON wrappers, URL encoding, temp files, logging, version compare, shell escaping.
Create commands.vim: intent table, parse positional/subcommands/options, dispatch, error formatting.
Create health.vim and a headless smoke test script.
Add doc/vim-opencode.txt skeleton and syntax/ftplugin placeholders.
acceptance: :Opencode help works.
Config merge and validation errors are clear.
Command completion works for subcommands.
Headless Vim sources the plugin without errors.
risks: Vim9 whitespace and type rules are stricter than legacy Vimscript.
Command completion can be slow if it calls the network; cache catalogs.

implementation_pathways.name: Transport, discovery and connection
implementation_pathways.goal: Find or start a server, probe the protocol, make authenticated requests and subscribe to SSE.
steps: Implement curl argv building for GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE, headers, auth and JSON body.
Implement request execution with job_start and temp files; add timeouts and cancellation.
Implement discovery: configured URL -> service.json/service-<channel>.json newest first -> server.start callback -> poll for five seconds.
Implement V2 probe GET /api/info and store version/protocol.
Implement SSE subscription GET /api/event with chunk accumulation, frame parsing, heartbeats and reconnect/backoff.
Track requests and the SSE job on the connection; clean up on VimLeavePre.
Add :Opencode server status/connect/disconnect and health checks.
acceptance: Connects to a running V2 service and reports its version.
Starts a server via a configured start callback and reconnects.
Receives server.connected and session.status events.
Heartbeat expiry triggers a visible reconnect attempt.
No orphan curl jobs after :qa.
risks: SSE chunks can split UTF-8 and JSON; parse on frame boundaries, not arbitrary chunk boundaries.
curl stderr/exit codes need careful mapping to useful errors.
Vim9 job callback functions must be reachable (global g: functions or string names); script-local def callbacks need wrappers.

implementation_pathways.name: Context, prompt, ask and operator
implementation_pathways.goal: A nickjvandyke-parity workflow: context-aware prompt, ask and operator.
steps: Implement Context capture: buffer/win/cursor, visual range/kind, selection text, scratch-buffer fallback.
Implement placeholder scanner with longest-match-first and input/output segment lists.
Implement built-ins: @this, @buffer, @buffers, @visible, @quickfix, @marks, @diagnostics (quickfix/location list).
Implement path:line:column formatting relative to cwd; normalize reversed selections.
Implement session resolution: most recent non-archived root session for cwd.
Implement prompt submission and trailing ... behavior.
Implement ask via input() with customlist completion, or a small popup input.
Implement operator() with operatorfunc and g@.
Add :Opencode ask/prompt/operator and visual mappings.
acceptance: @this sends the selection or cursor location.
A visual selection is highlighted and can be resumed after cancel/error.
Trailing ... opens ask.
Dot-repeat works for the operator mapping.
Prompt errors leave the editor state intact.
risks: Diagnostics semantics differ without vim.diagnostic; document the quickfix-backed behavior.
input() blocks the event loop; do not rely on streaming during ask.
Path encoding and Windows drive letters need tests.

implementation_pathways.name: Split panel and streaming renderer
implementation_pathways.goal: A persistent panel that streams a readable transcript without blocking input.
steps: Create output/input scratch buffers and a split layout with focus/toggle/zoom.
Implement a session transcript model: ordered messages, parts, tool/reasoning/text roles.
Implement a formatter that emits line arrays plus highlight ranges and fold ranges.
Batch-write lines on a timer (for example 40-80 ms); avoid per-token writes.
Use prop_add/prop_add_list for highlights and virtual text; use manual folds for tools/reasoning.
Keep the bottom anchored when the user is at the bottom; preserve the top otherwise.
Add navigation: next/prev message, next/prev user message, jump to file at cursor.
Add a minimal input buffer submit flow and prompt history.
Add :Opencode toggle/open input/open output/close.
acceptance: Streaming text appears smoothly without flicker.
The user can type in the input buffer while output streams.
Folds for tool output can be opened/closed.
Scrolling up is not yanked back to the bottom by new tokens.
Closing/reopening the panel preserves the draft and scroll position.
risks: Text property/virtual text behavior differs from extmarks; test zero-width and end-of-line cases.
Manual fold management can conflict with syntax folding; isolate with foldmethod=manual.
Frequent buffer writes are expensive; batch and skip work when the panel is hidden.

implementation_pathways.name: Sessions, models, agents and commands
implementation_pathways.goal: Manage more than the most recent session and select models/agents/commands.
steps: Implement list/create/rename/delete/fork/revert operations in the V2 adapter.
Add a popup_menu session picker with project/global scope and a preview line.
Add model/provider/agent list fetch and selection; persist favorites/recent choices.
Add server command list, argument prompt and execution.
Add slash-like command navigation in the input (a popup list, no literal / DSL required).
Add basic child/parent session navigation if the server exposes it.
acceptance: The session picker lists and opens sessions for the current directory.
A chosen model/agent is applied to the next prompt.
A server command runs with optional arguments.
Favorites/recent choices survive a restart.
risks: The V2 catalog shapes can change; ignore unknown fields and fail softly.
Session scoping by directory is subtle; always send both the directory query and header.
Popup previews are limited; do not block the release on rich previews.

implementation_pathways.name: Permissions and edit diff review
implementation_pathways.goal: Safely approve/reject actions and review proposed edits.
steps: Listen for permission.asked/question.asked and create pending records.
Implement Once/Always/Reject dialogs with popup_menu; support multiple pending requests by index.
Reply via /api/session/{id}/permission/{requestID}/reply and clear optimistic state.
For edit requests with a single file and patch, write a temp patch, tabnew the target, and :diffpatch.
Install buffer-local da/dr/dp/do/q mappings; accept/reject the whole request; preserve native per-hunk behavior.
Close the diff tab on permission.replied.
Fall back to the generic permission dialog for multi-file or patch-less edits.
Add :Opencode permission accept/accept_all/deny.
acceptance: A permission request can be approved or rejected without leaving Vim.
A single-file edit opens a diff and da/dr reply correctly.
dp/do still perform native hunk operations.
The diff tab closes when the request is resolved elsewhere.
risks: Accepting a patch changes the working tree; make the semantics explicit and keep an undo path.
Multi-file edits cannot be previewed safely with this approach; do not silently approve.
The permission metadata shape is version-specific; fail closed and show the generic dialog.

implementation_pathways.name: Rich context engine and review feedback loop
implementation_pathways.goal: Close the gap to sudo-tee's context and review workflow.
steps: Add current-file, cursor-window, whole-buffer and git-diff context sources.
Add per-session sent-context hashes and re-send only changed items.
Add review comments with file/line/range and a stable reference id.
Attach review comments to prompts and render them in a context bar/statusline.
Add a session-diff browser using GET /api/session/{id}/diff and the native diff view.
Add inline comment creation with signs/virtual text and next/prev comment navigation.
Add a context item toggle UI (#-like picker) and clear actions.
acceptance: Unchanged context is not re-sent.
Comments on a review diff appear in the next prompt.
A stale comment includes a warning and current code context.
The context bar accurately reflects what will be sent.
risks: Context heuristics can surprise users; make them visible and easy to disable.
Review comments anchored to snapshots can drift after local edits.
Git operations can be slow in large repos; run asynchronously and cache.

implementation_pathways.name: Quick chat and inline edits
implementation_pathways.goal: Make a small edit in place without opening the panel.
steps: Capture the cursor line +/-N or the visual range.
Create a temporary V2 session with replacement-oriented instructions.
Submit the range and optional context tags (#buffer, #file, #git_diff, #errors, #warnings).
Observe assistant text; accumulate until idle.
Replace only the target lines and rely on :undo for recovery.
Show a spinner with virtual text or a statusline message; support cancellation.
Delete the temporary session unless a debug flag keeps it.
acceptance: A visual selection is replaced by the model's reply.
u restores the previous lines.
<C-c> cancels and leaves the buffer untouched.
The temporary session is removed by default.
risks: Partial replacements can break syntax; default to whole-line replacement.
A late reply after cancellation must be discarded by request id.
Temporary session creation can be slow; show progress.

implementation_pathways.name: Panel tabs, persistence and extensibility
implementation_pathways.goal: Support multiple conversations, restore state, and expose user hooks.
steps: Add internal PanelTab objects with session/directory/draft/context.
Add a one-line tab strip buffer or statusline segment with next/prev/select/close.
Persist project-scoped tab metadata and restore valid tabs on first use.
Add prompt history JSONL and up/down navigation.
Add user hooks: on_file_edited, on_status, on_permission, on_question, on_done.
Add a local command registry and optional tool formatter registry.
Add a prompt guard callback.
acceptance: Two tabs keep independent drafts and sessions.
Restarting Vim restores valid tabs for the project.
Hooks fire once per event and errors are isolated.
A blocked prompt explains why.
risks: Project grouping is hard to get right for worktrees and remote paths.
Persistence can resurrect stale or deleted sessions; validate aggressively.
Too many hooks increase compatibility burden; document stability.

implementation_pathways.name: V1 adapter and protocol hardening
implementation_pathways.goal: Support both OpenCode generations without leaking differences into the UI.
steps: Define the adapter interface precisely from the V2 implementation.
Add V1 health /global/health and operations for sessions/messages/commands/permissions/questions.
Add V1 event subscription /global/event and normalization to the shared event shape.
Gate features that are unsupported and report clear errors.
Add contract tests against recorded fixtures for both versions.
Add a startup drift check against /openapi.json where available.
acceptance: The same prompt/context/event flows work against V1 and V2.
Unsupported operations fail with an actionable message.
Recorded event fixtures normalize to the same internal shapes.
risks: V1 is legacy and may not be worth the maintenance cost.
The event and message shapes are meaningfully different; normalization is real work.
Feature parity is not achievable for V2-only endpoints.

implementation_pathways.name: Hardening, performance, packaging and release
implementation_pathways.goal: Make the plugin dependable on real projects and slow servers.
steps: Add headless tests with assert_equal and fixture servers.
Add :defcompile and source checks to CI.
Profile transcript rendering on long sessions; cap rendered messages and skip hidden panels.
Add request timeouts, cancellation, reconnect backoff and clear error messages.
Test Windows/macOS path and clipboard behavior if those platforms are in scope.
Write help, configuration docs, event contract docs and troubleshooting.
Tag and package with a stable public API.
acceptance: CI passes on the minimum supported Vim 9.1 patch level.
A 1000-message transcript stays responsive.
Network failures do not leave orphan jobs or stuck UI.
A new user can install, connect and send a prompt from the docs alone.
risks: Vim9 compiler/version differences across distro builds.
No standard test framework; tests must be plain scripts.
Platform-specific shell tools undermine the vanilla promise.

alternative_pathways.name: Thin bridge only (nickjvandyke parity)
alternative_pathways.scope: P0 + P1 + P2 + P5; no panel, no tabs, no transcript.
pros: Fastest path to a useful plugin.
Small surface area and easy to test.
cons: No persistent conversation view; users must watch the OpenCode TUI.
Streaming is not visible while composing.
Less differentiated than the existing Neovim plugins.
alternative_pathways.recommended_if: The goal is a dependable Vim-native prompt bridge, not an IDE.

alternative_pathways.name: Panel-first subset (recommended)
alternative_pathways.scope: P0-P5 plus a minimal panel/renderer; defer tabs, review comments, quick chat and V1.
pros: Delivers the highest-value UX: streaming chat, context, commands, permissions and edit review.
Keeps the door open for sudo-tee-like features.
Still testable and shippable in a reasonable timeframe.
cons: Rendering and async complexity are the hard part.
No session tabs or rich review yet.
alternative_pathways.recommended_if: The goal is a daily-driver Vim client for OpenCode.

alternative_pathways.name: Full dual-protocol parity
alternative_pathways.scope: P0-P10 including tabs, rich context, review comments, quick chat, image paste and V1.
cons: Large maintenance burden in a smaller ecosystem.
Protocol drift and UI edge cases dominate.
alternative_pathways.recommended_if: There is a long-term maintainer and a clear user demand.

alternative_pathways.name: External helper sidecar
alternative_pathways.scope: A small Python/Go helper owns HTTP/SSE/state; Vim9 is a thin UI over JSON-RPC/stdin.
pros: Much easier async, HTTP, TLS and SSE.
Portable state machine and easier testing.
cons: Breaks the 'vanilla Vim 9.1 + curl only' constraint.
Adds a process to install and supervise.
alternative_pathways.recommended_if: The constraint is negotiable and reliability matters more than a single-language plugin.

milestones.outcome: Can connect, probe V2, make a request and receive SSE events in a log.
Ask/prompt/operator with placeholders, commands and events. Comparable to nickjvandyke's core.
Streaming panel, session/model pickers, permissions and edit diffs. Daily-driver candidate.
Rich context, review comments, quick chat, tabs, persistence and hooks.
V1 adapter, contract fixtures, performance work, docs and release.

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Treat the parser as a tested state machine; buffer by frame; heartbeat deadline; capped exponential backoff; integration test against a local SSE server.
Use global g: callback functions or string names; keep callbacks tiny; pass state through g: dicts/ids. Verified in a smoke test.
Batch writes on a timer, cap rendered messages, skip hidden panels, avoid per-token full rebuilds, profile long sessions.
Use prop_add_list, avoid overlapping properties, isolate manual folds, test end-of-line virtual text and zero-width cases.
Use syntax/conceal for Markdown and complete()/popup for completion; set expectations in docs.
Read quickfix/location lists; document optional integration with external lint/LSP plugins; do not claim diagnostic parity.
Defer; detect wl-paste/xclip/pngpaste/PowerShell; shell out to base64; fail with a clear message.
V2-first; adapter boundary; ignore unknown fields; contract tests with recorded fixtures; clear unsupported-feature errors.
Use a normal input buffer for the panel; reserve input() for one-shot asks; document the tradeoff.
Fail closed on unknown metadata; never silently approve multi-file edits; make apply/reject semantics explicit; rely on undo.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Scope creep toward full sudo-tee parity
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Ship the thin bridge and panel first; put tabs/review comments/quick chat/image/V1 behind later milestones.

unit: JSON/request encoding, URL encoding, path maps, placeholder scanner, event reducer, version compare.
Use plain Vim9 test scripts with assert_equal/assert_true and v:errors.
integration: Local Python HTTP/SSE fixture server for discovery, requests, heartbeats, reconnect and events.
Recorded V1/V2 payload fixtures for normalization and contract tests.
A fake server that returns 401/404/500 to verify error paths.
ui: Headless buffer tests for renderer line/property/fold output.
Manual smoke matrix for split layout, input submit, popup menus, diff review and permission dialogs.
Long-session performance test with a synthetic transcript.
ci: source plugin from a clean runtimepath
run on the minimum supported Vim 9.1 patch level and a recent build

recommendation.primary: Build pathway B: a V2-first, Vim9-native core plus a split-panel transcript, and defer full sudo-tee parity. Start with P0-P2 (thin bridge) to prove transport/context/prompt, then P3-P5 (panel, pickers, permissions, diff). Treat P6-P9 as later milestones.
reasons: It delivers a genuinely useful Vim client in a few weeks instead of a multi-month parity project.
It maximizes reuse of native Vim behavior (diff, operator, popup, syntax) and minimizes Neovim-only gaps.
It keeps a clean architecture for later session tabs, review comments, quick chat and V1.
It avoids the two biggest traps: a literal extmark/Treesitter/LSP port and a full Promise/async port.
first_three_deliverables: A connection that can discover/start V2, probe /api/info, send a prompt and receive events.
Ask/prompt/operator with @ placeholders and a select menu for server commands.
A split panel with debounced streaming output and a normal input buffer.
decision_points: If the user only needs prompt/context/diff, stop after M1 and skip the panel.
If reliability matters more than a single-language plugin, consider the sidecar pathway D.
If V1 users matter, add P9 only after the V2 event/reducer layer is stable.

open_questions: Which OpenCode generation is the primary target: V2 only, or must V1 work on day one?
Is a persistent panel required, or is a thin prompt/context bridge enough?
Are external binaries acceptable beyond opencode and curl (for clipboard images, base64, fuzzy finders)?
Which platforms are in scope: Linux only, or Windows/macOS too?
Is a Python/Go sidecar acceptable if it materially improves reliability?
How much of sudo-tee's review-comment workflow is required for the first release?
Should the plugin expose a stable Lua-like extension API, or only Ex commands, functions and autocmds?
